title: SYSTEMATIC-SIGNAL: can a free signal predict where the bootstrap is confidently wrong? (the fix for TIER-HONEST's flaw; zero calls)
question: On the 891 (anchor, model-pair) edges from RESOLVE-CALIB, each with the arena's bootstrap P(A above B) and the key's verdict, are the wrong-direction edges distinguishable from the right ones by three predictors computable without extra calls: (a) the two models' answer-agreement rate within the anchor, (b) the incumbent reference's accuracy in the anchor, (c) the key gap between the two models (the sanity check, unavailable at deployment)?

criteria.text: PRIMARY: among edges the arena CALLS at the 0.975 threshold, the mean answer-agreement of wrong-direction edges minus that of correct ones is positive with a bootstrap CI excluding zero
criteria.denominator: 739 called of 891 edges at 0.975, 8 wrong-direction (the key-gap >= 0.02 filtered denominator; honest denominator per the correction: 920 edges / 748 called / 11 wrong)

criteria.text: the same for reference accuracy, expected NEGATIVE
criteria.value: 0.765 vs 0.852, -0.088 [-0.111, -0.052]; key gap -0.290 [-0.318, -0.261] as the sanity check [CORRECTED by SYSTEMATIC-BUDGET: reference accuracy is key-derived, not a free signal]

criteria.text: a two-predictor logistic of wrong-direction on agreement and reference accuracy: does either survive the other
criteria.value: answer-agreement +1.511 +- 0.215 (z +7.0), reference accuracy -0.798 +- 0.190 (z -4.2); each survives conditioning on the other
criteria.denominator: all 891 edges, 44 wrong [18 of the 44 not established by McNemar: SYSTEMATIC-BUDGET (c)]

criteria.text: OPERATING POINT: if a signal works, the agreement threshold at which declining edges would have removed the wrong calls, and how many correct calls that costs
criteria.value: declining at agreement > 0.70 removes 4 of 8 wrong calls and costs 97 of 731 correct; at 0.85 removes 2 and costs 11: as a HARD GATE the signal is poor (ledger chip GATE FAILS); the table was the wrong instrument for a continuous widener

predictions.text: answer-agreement is the stronger signal and gives a difference of +0.05 to +0.15
predictions.value: +0.267 [+0.150, +0.374]: the stronger signal (HELD in direction), the size too small by a factor of two (the registered band FAILED)

predictions.text: reference accuracy is weaker and may not survive
predictions.value: it survives the two-predictor logistic (z -4.2); weaker than agreement (z +7.0)

predictions.text: a usable operating point declines under 15% of called edges to remove most wrong ones
predictions.value: 0.70 threshold: 4 of 8 removed at a cost of 97 of 731 correct (13.3% declined, half removed); 0.85: 2 of 8 at 11 correct

predictions.text: POWER CAVEAT: ~6 wrong edges at the 0.975 threshold; a null must be reported as UNDERPOWERED
predictions.value: did not bite: 8 wrong edges, the effect large enough (+0.267) that its interval clears zero; the logistic uses all 44 wrong edges

falsifier.text: if none of the three signals predicts a wrong call, the design's fix for its worst flaw (RESOLVE's systematic budget) does not work and the tier map cannot be trusted at the boundaries that matter

brackets.text: three ways, before any of this was published outside the repo: (a) CALLING REFERENCE ACCURACY A 'FREE' SIGNAL WAS WRONG. It is free of extra CALLS and it is KEY-DERIVED (rejudge_reference.references() returns the reference graded against the answer key); it cannot be computed at deployment on unkeyed data; the shipped budget therefore carries answer agreement ONLY, even though adding reference accuracy fits materially better (LOAO deviance 193.55 against 216.94). (b) THE DENOMINATOR IS SELECTED: the 0.82% / 1.08% wrong-call rates rest on the key-gap >= 0.02 filter, unavailable at deployment and dropping edges that are far MORE often wrong; honest denominator 920 edges, 60 wrong, 748 called with 11 wrong = 1.47%. (c) 41% OF THE WRONG-DIRECTION LABELS ARE NOT ESTABLISHED: exact two-sided McNemar adjudicates 809 of the 891; 18 of the 44 'wrong' edges sit among the 82 it cannot; the effect survives (b1 3.3133 -> 2.1430 on established edges only).

plain_description.what: On 891 subject-by-model-pair comparisons, checks whether signals available without extra calls predict where the arena is confidently wrong about which model is better. The signals are how often the two models give the same answer, and how accurate the reference is.
plain_description.why: Confidence intervals were sometimes confidently wrong. This looks for a cheap warning signal to widen uncertainty where errors are likely.
plain_description.information: A predictive signal would let the system flag risky comparisons; none would leave those errors hidden. Result: confirmed as stated, but corrected. High answer agreement between the two models predicts wrong calls. Reference accuracy also predicts them, but it needs the answer key, so only answer agreement can be used in practice. As a hard cut-off the signal is poor, so it is used as a continuous widening instead. Ruled history rather than evidence (older question pool).
